project.name: labConnect
project.description: Multi-role medical laboratory platform (Django REST backend, React + Vite web dashboard, React Native + Expo mobile app) with JWT auth, supporting analyses, appointments, notifications, inventory management, and CNAM reimbursement workflows.

nodes.name: App.jsx
nodes.summary: Root application component providing role-aware routing via Shell and Gate sub-components; Shell renders the main navigation layout and switches screens based on user roles and permissions, while Gate guards access and handles lab onboarding flow.

nodes.name: Shell
nodes.summary: Main authenticated layout shell that fetches sidebar badge counts, manages screen navigation state, and renders Sidebar, Topbar, and the active screen component based on the user's role and permissions.

nodes.name: Gate
nodes.summary: Authentication gate component that checks login state and onboarding status, redirecting unauthenticated users to Login and lab-less staff to Onboarding.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Top-level App component that wraps the Gate within an AuthProvider context.

nodes.name: api.js
nodes.summary: Central API client module providing JWT token management, authenticated fetch wrapper with auto-refresh, and domain-specific CRUD functions covering auth, labs, catalog, employees, orders, appointments, inventory, notifications, and results.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a lab-scoped singleton pattern via localStorage to scope all requests to the active lab; includes automatic JWT refresh with 401 retry.

nodes.name: ApiError
nodes.summary: Custom error class extending Error that carries HTTP status code and parsed response body for structured API error handling.

nodes.name: rawFetch
nodes.summary: Core authenticated fetch wrapper that attaches JWT access token headers, handles 401 responses by refreshing tokens and retrying once, and throws ApiError on non-2xx responses.

nodes.name: geocode
nodes.summary: Calls the Nominatim OpenStreetMap geocoding API to convert a text query into geographic coordinates.

nodes.name: reverseGeocode
nodes.summary: Calls the Nominatim reverse geocoding API to convert latitude/longitude coordinates into a human-readable address.

nodes.name: auth.jsx
nodes.summary: Authentication context provider and hook; AuthProvider hydrates user state from the API on mount and exposes login, Google OAuth login, and logout actions along with active lab selection.

nodes.name: AuthProvider
nodes.summary: React context provider that manages authentication state, exposes login/logout/switchLab actions, and hydrates user and lab data from the API on startup.

nodes.name: useAuth
nodes.summary: Custom hook providing access to the AuthContext; throws if used outside of AuthProvider.

nodes.name: AppointmentDetailModal.jsx
nodes.summary: Modal component for viewing and progressing an appointment through its lifecycle steps (pending, sample collected, results entered, validated), displaying patient info, test items, and allowing status transitions.

nodes.name: AppointmentDetailModal
nodes.summary: Main modal component that renders appointment details, step progress indicators, test item list, patient avatar, and action buttons for advancing appointment status through the lab workflow.

nodes.name: FinanceTab.jsx
nodes.summary: Finance tab component embedded in the Dashboard that fetches and displays daily/weekly appointment revenue summaries, CNAM reimbursement breakdowns, and invoice access with filtering capabilities.

nodes.name: FinanceTab
nodes.summary: React component fetching financial data from the API and rendering revenue summaries, CNAM status breakdowns, and appointment invoice rows with search and date filtering.

nodes.name: InvoiceModal.jsx
nodes.summary: Modal component that fetches and displays the detailed invoice for an appointment, showing test items, pricing, CNAM coverage, and payment status badge.

nodes.name: InvoiceModal
nodes.summary: React component that loads invoice data for a given appointment UUID and renders a structured breakdown of test items, totals, CNAM deduction, and payment status.

nodes.name: LabSwitcher.jsx
nodes.summary: Dropdown component in the Topbar that allows staff with access to multiple labs to switch the active laboratory context.

nodes.name: MapPicker.jsx
nodes.summary: Interactive map component using Leaflet that lets users pick a geographic location by clicking or searching, with reverse geocoding to display the selected address.

nodes.name: MapPicker
nodes.summary: Leaflet-based map picker component with address search using geocoding, click-to-pin location, and reverse geocoding to surface the selected address label to the parent.

nodes.name: Misc.jsx
nodes.summary: Shared micro-components module exporting CatBadge for category labels, PermRibbon for permission display, and FullScreenLoader for loading states.

nodes.name: Modal.jsx
nodes.summary: Generic modal overlay component with close button, backdrop click-to-close, and title slot used as the base modal wrapper across the application.

nodes.name: NotificationsBell.jsx
nodes.summary: Bell icon component in the Topbar that polls for unread notification counts, displays a dropdown list of notifications with relative timestamps, and allows marking individual or all notifications as read.

nodes.name: NotificationsBell
nodes.summary: Polling notification bell that fetches unread count on an interval, loads full notifications on open, and supports marking items read via API calls.

nodes.name: RoleSwitcher.jsx
nodes.summary: Topbar dropdown component enabling multi-role staff users to switch their active role view, with click-outside dismissal.

nodes.name: Sidebar.jsx
nodes.summary: Navigation sidebar component rendering role-filtered menu items with badge counts for pending actions, supporting mobile toggle and active screen highlighting.

nodes.name: Switch.jsx
nodes.summary: Minimal toggle switch input component used for boolean settings fields across the application.

nodes.name: Topbar.jsx
nodes.summary: Top navigation bar component composing LabSwitcher, RoleSwitcher, and NotificationsBell alongside a hamburger menu toggle for mobile layouts.

nodes.name: WalkInModal.jsx
nodes.summary: Walk-in appointment creation modal allowing staff to search for and add tests from the catalog, enter patient details, configure CNAM coverage, select appointment type (in-lab vs home visit), and submit the order.

nodes.name: WalkInModal
nodes.summary: Large form modal for creating walk-in orders with patient info, test catalog search and selection, CNAM flag, appointment type, and scheduled date/time fields.

nodes.name: constants.js
nodes.summary: Application-wide constants and utility functions module exporting role definitions, permission maps, category lists, UI helpers (initials, avatar classes), and lab configuration defaults used across all screens.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines permissionsFor() which maps a role string to a permissions object — the key RBAC primitive driving conditional UI rendering throughout the app.

nodes.name: permissionsFor
nodes.summary: Maps a staff role identifier to a structured permissions object controlling which UI actions and screens are available to that role.

nodes.name: useClickOutside.js
nodes.summary: Custom React hook that attaches a mousedown event listener to detect clicks outside a given DOM ref and invokes a callback, used for closing dropdowns.

nodes.name: icons.jsx
nodes.summary: Icon component module that renders Heroicons SVG icons by name via the I export, providing a thin wrapper around a large static icon map used across all UI components.

nodes.name: main.jsx
nodes.summary: Vite/React application entry point that mounts the App component into the DOM root with React 18 createRoot.

nodes.name: Analyses.jsx
nodes.summary: Main analyses screen managing lab orders across in-progress and completed states, with sub-components for result entry (ResultEntryModal), result validation (ValidationModal), PDF download, and sample management.

nodes.name: ResultEntryModal
nodes.summary: Modal form component for laboratory staff to enter test result values for an order, submitting to the API and triggering a parent refresh on success.

nodes.name: ValidationModal
nodes.summary: Large modal for biologists to review entered results, add comments, and validate or reject the final result for each order, with full result history display.

nodes.name: Analyses
nodes.summary: Primary screen component displaying paginated order lists filtered by status, supporting sample reception/rejection, result entry, validation workflows, and PDF result downloads.

nodes.name: Dashboard.jsx
nodes.summary: Main dashboard screen showing today's appointment list with status badges, walk-in creation, appointment detail modal, invoice access, and an embedded FinanceTab for revenue tracking.

nodes.name: Dashboard
nodes.summary: React screen component fetching today's appointments and rendering an appointment list, status filtering tabs, walk-in modal, appointment detail modal, invoice modal, and finance tab.

nodes.name: Inventory.jsx
nodes.summary: Inventory management screen with item CRUD (ItemModal), stock movement recording (MovementModal), and a table view of lab supplies with quantity tracking.

nodes.name: ItemModal
nodes.summary: Modal form for creating or editing inventory items including name, category, unit, and initial quantity fields.

nodes.name: MovementModal
nodes.summary: Modal for recording inventory movements (in/out) for an item, displaying movement history and submitting new quantity adjustments with notes.

nodes.name: Inventory
nodes.summary: Main inventory screen listing all lab supplies with search, category filter, add/edit/delete actions, and movement tracking per item.

nodes.name: Login.jsx
nodes.summary: Authentication screen providing email/password staff login form and Google OAuth sign-in button, with error display and loading state.

nodes.name: Login
nodes.summary: Login page component handling credential form submission, Google OAuth flow via Google Identity Services script, and delegating authentication to the useAuth hook.

nodes.name: NursesMap.jsx
nodes.summary: Nurse management screen displaying today's home visit appointments on a Leaflet map, allowing supervisors to assign nurses to visits and track visit status.

nodes.name: AssignNurseModal
nodes.summary: Modal for selecting an available nurse and assigning them to a specific home visit appointment via the API.

nodes.name: NursesMap
nodes.summary: Main screen component rendering a Leaflet map of home visit locations, a sidebar list of today's visits with status and nurse assignment, and real-time-ish polling for updates.

nodes.name: Onboarding.jsx
nodes.summary: Lab onboarding screen for new staff without an assigned lab, allowing them to create a new laboratory or join an existing one by providing name, location, and address details.

nodes.name: Settings.jsx
nodes.summary: Lab settings screen for administrators to update laboratory configuration including name, address, location via MapPicker, contact details, and CNAM/home-visit feature toggles.

nodes.name: Staff.jsx
nodes.summary: Staff management screen for administrators to view, invite, update roles, and deactivate lab employees, with a modal form for editing staff details.

nodes.name: StaffModal
nodes.summary: Modal form for inviting new staff or editing an existing employee's name and role assignments within the lab.

nodes.name: Staff
nodes.summary: Main staff management screen listing all lab employees with role badges, deactivation toggles, and invite/edit actions delegating to StaffModal.

nodes.name: Stats.jsx
nodes.summary: Statistics screen fetching aggregated lab performance data and rendering horizontal bar charts for top tests, daily appointment volume bars, and summary KPI cards.

nodes.name: Stats
nodes.summary: Main stats screen that loads analytics data from the API and renders KPI summary cards, top-test bar charts, and a day-of-week appointment volume visualization.

nodes.name: Tests.jsx
nodes.summary: Test catalog management screen for creating, editing, and deleting lab tests with pricing and category, including a preset picker for quick population from standard test templates.

nodes.name: TestModal
nodes.summary: Modal form for creating or editing a lab test with name, category, price, turnaround time, and CNAM coverage fields.

nodes.name: Tests
nodes.summary: Main test catalog screen displaying all lab tests with search and category filtering, supporting add, edit, and delete actions via TestModal.

nodes.name: admin.py
nodes.summary: Registers all accounts-domain models (User, PatientProfile, StaffProfile, OTPCode, TrustedDevice) with the Django admin site, configuring list displays and search fields for operational use.

nodes.name: UserAdmin
nodes.summary: Custom Django admin class for the User model with list display, search, and ordering configuration.

nodes.name: bootstrap_chief.py
nodes.summary: Django management command that provisions a fully-configured lab-chief user together with an associated Laboratory and StaffProfile in a single atomic step, intended for initial environment setup.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Management command class that accepts CLI arguments for user and lab details, then creates or updates the lab-chief user, their Laboratory, and StaffProfile records.

nodes.name: create_chef.py
nodes.summary: Django management command for creating or updating a lab-chief user account with email/phone credentials and assigning the lab-chief group role.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Management command class that validates and upserts a lab-chief user, assigning the appropriate Django Group.

nodes.name: seed_roles.py
nodes.summary: Lightweight management command that bootstraps all role-based Django Groups (patient, secretary, nurse, technician, biologist, lab_chief) required by the platform permission system.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Management command that calls get_or_create for each role group name from the RoleNames constant.

nodes.name: managers.py
nodes.summary: Provides the custom UserManager that replaces the default Django user manager, enforcing phone-number normalization and supporting both regular and superuser creation flows.

nodes.name: UserManager
nodes.summary: Custom Django manager that normalizes phone numbers and email, builds User instances, and enforces is_staff / is_superuser requirements for superuser creation.

nodes.name: 0001_initial.py
nodes.summary: Initial Django migration that creates the User, PatientProfile, StaffProfile, OTPCode, TrustedDevice, and TOTPDevice database tables for the accounts application.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Core identity and authentication models for the platform, defining the custom User (phone-primary), PatientProfile, StaffProfile, OTPCode (hashed, expiring), TrustedDevice (biometric tokens), and TOTPDevice.

nodes.name: User
nodes.summary: Custom AbstractBaseUser that uses phone number as the primary identifier, supports email as optional secondary, normalizes phone on save, and exposes full/short name helpers.

nodes.name: OTPCode
nodes.summary: Represents a one-time password code stored as a salted SHA-256 hash; provides issue() factory, verify() consumer, and is_expired() guard methods.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses secrets.token_hex for the salt and hashlib.sha256 for hashing — no third-party OTP library.

nodes.name: TrustedDevice
nodes.summary: Tracks biometric-linked device tokens per phone/device_id pair; issue() creates or refreshes a hashed token, verify() uses secrets.compare_digest for constant-time comparison.

nodes.name: PatientProfile
nodes.summary: Extended profile for patient users storing insurance number, CNAM status, gender, birth date, and optional GIS home location.

nodes.name: StaffProfile
nodes.summary: Profile linking a User to a Laboratory with role metadata, supporting soft-delete inherited from BaseModel and an active manager.

nodes.name: TOTPDevice
nodes.summary: Stores a TOTP secret per user, tracking confirmation status and the last used step to prevent replay attacks.

nodes.name: serializers.py
nodes.summary: DRF serializers for OTP request/verification flows, full user profile read/write (including PatientProfile and GIS point), and login serializers for staff, Google, and Firebase authentication strategies.

nodes.name: UserMeSerializer
nodes.summary: Full user profile serializer that reads roles from Django Groups, extracts GIS coordinates from PatientProfile location, and on update merges profile data including optional lat/lng into a PostGIS Point.

nodes.name: OTPRequestSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for OTP request payloads, validating and normalizing the phone number via User.normalize_phone.

nodes.name: OTPVerifySerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for OTP verification payloads, validating phone and the 6-digit code.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package initializer for the accounts services sub-package, enabling Python module resolution.

nodes.name: firebase.py
nodes.summary: Pure-Python Firebase JWT verification service that fetches and caches Google's public RSA certificates, then decodes and validates Firebase ID tokens including audience, issuer, and expiry claims.
nodes.languageNotes: Does not use the firebase-admin SDK; instead fetches Google public certs via urllib and verifies JWTs with PyJWT + cryptography, with a simple in-process cache keyed by cert kid.

nodes.name: verify_id_token
nodes.summary: Verifies a Firebase ID token by extracting the key ID, loading the corresponding RSA public key, decoding the JWT, and validating audience, issuer, subject, and email-verified claims.

nodes.name: _load_public_keys
nodes.summary: Fetches Google's Firebase public key certificates from the JWKS endpoint, parses max-age from Cache-Control headers, and populates an in-memory key cache.

nodes.name: otp.py
nodes.summary: OTP delivery abstraction layer that defines OTPProvider interface with Mock, Twilio SMS, and WhatsApp concrete implementations, plus factory get_provider() and 6-digit code generator.

nodes.name: TwilioSMSProvider
nodes.summary: OTP provider that sends SMS messages via the Twilio client, using a rendered bilingual message body.

nodes.name: get_provider
nodes.summary: Factory that returns the configured OTP provider instance based on the OTP_PROVIDER Django setting, raising RuntimeError for unknown values.

nodes.name: tokens.py
nodes.summary: Custom SimpleJWT token classes that embed the user's role group names into the JWT payload, enabling client-side role awareness without extra API calls.

nodes.name: LabConnectRefreshToken
nodes.summary: Refresh token subclass that overrides for_user() to inject a 'roles' claim containing all Django Group names for the user.

nodes.name: urls.py
nodes.summary: URL router for the accounts app, mapping OTP, login, logout, biometric, TOTP, and employee management endpoints to their respective view classes.

nodes.name: views.py
nodes.summary: Core authentication views handling OTP request/verify, staff and patient email login, Google OAuth login (both patient and staff), Firebase login, user profile retrieval, and logout with JWT blacklisting.

nodes.name: OTPRequestView
nodes.summary: API view that invalidates any pending OTPs, generates a fresh code, persists it via OTPCode.issue(), and dispatches it through the configured OTP provider.

nodes.name: OTPVerifyView
nodes.summary: API view that verifies an OTP code, auto-creates a patient account on first use, and returns JWT access+refresh tokens with user profile data.

nodes.name: StaffLoginView
nodes.summary: API view for staff credential-based login, enforcing the staff profile check before issuing JWT tokens.

nodes.name: FirebaseLoginView
nodes.summary: API view that verifies a Firebase ID token, auto-provisions a patient account using the token's email/name claims, and returns JWT tokens.

nodes.name: PatientGoogleLoginView
nodes.summary: API view for patient Google OAuth login that verifies the Google ID token, auto-provisions a patient account, and returns JWT tokens.

nodes.name: GoogleLoginView
nodes.summary: Staff-only Google login view that verifies the Google ID token, looks up the existing staff account by email, checks staff group membership, and issues JWT tokens.

nodes.name: MeView
nodes.summary: RetrieveUpdateAPIView that returns or updates the authenticated user's profile, auto-creating PatientProfile on first access.

nodes.name: LogoutView
nodes.summary: API view that blacklists the provided refresh token to invalidate the session server-side.

nodes.name: verify_google_token
nodes.summary: Helper that validates a Google OAuth ID token against Google's tokeninfo endpoint and returns the decoded claims dict.

nodes.name: views_biometric.py
nodes.summary: API views implementing the biometric authentication flow: device enrollment check, token issuance (register), login with hashed-token verification, and device revocation.

nodes.name: BiometricRegisterView
nodes.summary: API view that registers a biometric device by issuing and storing a hashed TrustedDevice token tied to the user's phone and device ID.

nodes.name: BiometricLoginView
nodes.summary: API view that authenticates a user via their biometric device token, updating the last-seen timestamp on success and returning JWT tokens.

nodes.name: BiometricCheckView
nodes.summary: API view that checks whether a given phone/device_id pair has a registered and non-revoked TrustedDevice record.

nodes.name: BiometricRevokeView
nodes.summary: Authenticated API view that soft-revokes a TrustedDevice record for the requesting user's device ID.

nodes.name: views_employees.py
nodes.summary: Staff and employee management views including nurse listing, employee invitation (with user auto-provisioning), employee profile update, and soft-delete, all scoped to the requesting user's laboratory.

nodes.name: EmployeeInviteView
nodes.summary: API view that validates an invitation payload, auto-creates a User if needed, creates a StaffProfile, assigns the requested role groups, and returns the serialized profile.

nodes.name: EmployeeViewSet
nodes.summary: ModelViewSet for staff profiles scoped to the current lab; supports listing, role/profile update, and soft-delete with group cleanup.

nodes.name: NurseListView
nodes.summary: Read-only API view listing all active nurse profiles in the current laboratory, serialized for assignment UIs.

nodes.name: EmployeeInviteSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer validating employee invitation payloads, normalizing phone, and deduplicating the roles list.

nodes.name: StaffProfileSerializer
nodes.summary: Read serializer for StaffProfile that annotates role group names and a boolean TOTP-enabled flag.

nodes.name: views_totp.py
nodes.summary: TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) setup, confirmation, verification, and device-deletion API views for staff two-factor authentication, backed by a pyotp-compatible service layer.

nodes.name: TOTPSetupView
nodes.summary: API view that generates a new TOTP secret, stores it as an unconfirmed TOTPDevice, and returns the provisioning URI and QR code base64 image.

nodes.name: TOTPConfirmView
nodes.summary: API view that confirms a pending TOTPDevice by verifying the user-submitted TOTP code against the stored secret.

nodes.name: TOTPVerifyView
nodes.summary: API view for step-up 2FA verification; validates a TOTP code and returns a new JWT pair with a 2fa_verified payload claim on success.

nodes.name: TOTPDeviceDeleteView
nodes.summary: API view that soft-deletes the user's active TOTPDevice, disabling TOTP authentication.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Appointment model with VisitType and AppointmentStatus enumerations, supporting both clinic and home visits with GIS location, CNAM coverage, assigned nurse, and fee calculation.

nodes.name: Appointment
nodes.summary: Core appointment model linking patient, laboratory, optional nurse, and sample collection; tracks status lifecycle, CNAM eligibility, and home-visit GPS coordinates.

nodes.name: serializers.py
nodes.summary: DRF serializers for appointment read (with CNAM and fee aggregation), creation (with walk-in patient auto-provisioning and test-order building), and status transitions.

nodes.name: AppointmentSerializer
nodes.summary: Read serializer for Appointment that computes GIS coordinates, patient/nurse display names, nested order items, total fees in MRU, patient-due amount, and CNAM-covered amount.

nodes.name: AppointmentCreateSerializer
nodes.summary: Write serializer that validates patient identity (walk-in phone or authenticated user), resolves the laboratory, builds Sample and TestOrder records in a transaction, and handles CNAM pricing splits.

nodes.name: urls.py
nodes.summary: Minimal URL configuration for the appointments app, registering the AppointmentViewSet router and custom action routes.

nodes.name: views.py
nodes.summary: Appointment ViewSet with role-aware queryset scoping, nurse assignment, sample tube labelling, appointment cancellation, and status-change transitions that cascade to Sample and TestOrder records with push notifications.

nodes.name: AppointmentViewSet
nodes.summary: Full-featured ModelViewSet for appointments; filters by role (patient sees own, staff sees lab scope), provides mine/home_visits/assign_nurse/set_tubes/cancel/change_status actions, and fires push notifications on transitions.

nodes.name: IsPatientOrStaff
nodes.summary: DRF permission class that allows access to patients (no 2FA required) or any staff role with 2FA verified.

nodes.name: permissions.py
nodes.summary: Central permission classes and constants for the labConnect platform, defining role name strings, HasRole base permission, role-specific shortcuts (IsPatient, IsNurse, IsLabChief…), 2FA verification checks, and the current_lab_id request helper.

nodes.name: RoleNames
nodes.summary: String constant container for all platform role names (patient, secretary, nurse, technician, biologist, lab_chief) and an ALL_STAFF set.

nodes.name: HasRole
nodes.summary: Base DRF permission that checks whether the authenticated user belongs to any of the required_roles Django Groups.

nodes.name: Is2FAVerified
nodes.summary: DRF permission that checks the JWT payload for a 2fa_verified claim set to true.

nodes.name: IsStaffAnd2FA
nodes.summary: Composite DRF permission requiring the user to be any staff role AND have 2FA verified in their JWT.

nodes.name: LabScopedQuerysetMixin
nodes.summary: Mixin that overrides get_queryset() to filter by the lab ID from the current request, returning an empty queryset when no lab context is present.

nodes.name: current_lab_id
nodes.summary: Resolves the active laboratory ID for a request by checking the JWT payload, request headers, query params, and finally falling back to the staff's assigned laboratory.

nodes.name: admin.py
nodes.summary: Registers the Laboratory model with the Django admin, configuring list display, search, and location-aware map widget via djgeojson.

nodes.name: 0001_initial.py
nodes.summary: Initial Django migration creating the Laboratory table with PostGIS location field and all core laboratory attributes.

nodes.name: 0003_alter_laboratory_opening_hours.py
nodes.summary: Django migration altering the opening_hours JSON field on the Laboratory model to use the updated default structure.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Laboratory model with GIS location (PostGIS Point), opening hours (JSON), fee settings for home and emergency visits, CNAM support flag, and a slug identifier.

nodes.name: Laboratory
nodes.summary: Core laboratory entity with geolocation, opening hours JSON, home/emergency visit fees, CNAM support toggle, and soft-delete via BaseModel inheritance.

nodes.name: serializers.py
nodes.summary: DRF serializers for Laboratory list (with lat/lng extraction from PostGIS Point), detail view, opening-hours day validation, and full lab configuration update.

nodes.name: LaboratoryListSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for laboratory list view, extracting latitude/longitude from the PostGIS Point field via SerializerMethodFields.

nodes.name: LaboratoryConfigSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for updating laboratory configuration including opening hours validation (all-day or open/close time consistency), home visit fee, and emergency fee.

nodes.summary: Nested serializer that validates a single day's opening hours, ensuring that open/close times are consistent when the lab is not marked all-day.

nodes.name: urls.py
nodes.summary: URL router for the laboratories app, registering public lab search/nearby endpoints, employee management, and chef-scoped lab management routes.

nodes.name: views.py
nodes.summary: Laboratory views providing public geo-search (nearby by radius), lab-chief self-service (list, create, update opening hours and fees), and an inline serializer for laboratory creation.

nodes.name: LaboratoryPublicViewSet
nodes.summary: Read-only ViewSet for unauthenticated lab discovery, with a 'nearby' action that annotates laboratories with distance from a user-supplied GIS coordinate and filters within a radius.

nodes.name: ChefLaboratoryViewSet
nodes.summary: ViewSet for lab-chief users to list their laboratories, create new ones (with auto-StaffProfile creation), and update laboratory configuration via PATCH.

nodes.name: LaboratoryCreateSerializer
nodes.summary: Inline serializer for laboratory creation that auto-generates a unique slug, converts lat/lng to a PostGIS Point, and persists the Laboratory record.

nodes.name: App.js
nodes.summary: Root application component for the React Native mobile client, defining the full navigation tree with role-based shells: a patient tab navigator (Home, Bookings, Profile) and a nurse tab navigator (Route, Profile), wrapped in AuthProvider and NavigationContainer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses React Navigation's createNativeStackNavigator and createBottomTabNavigator. Role selection via pickRoleShell switches the whole shell at runtime. Custom font loading (Fredoka + Nunito) is handled before first render to avoid font flash.

nodes.name: MainTabs
nodes.summary: Bottom tab navigator for the patient role, exposing Home, Bookings, and Profile tabs with custom vectorial icons.

nodes.name: NurseTabs
nodes.summary: Bottom tab navigator for the nurse role, exposing Route (Tournée) and Profile tabs.

nodes.name: RootNav
nodes.summary: Top-level stack navigator that routes unauthenticated users to Login/SignUp and authenticated users to either the patient or nurse shell based on roles.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Default export and application root that loads Fredoka/Nunito fonts, patches the theme font objects, and renders the SafeAreaProvider + AuthProvider + NavigationContainer hierarchy.

nodes.name: BookingsScreen.js
nodes.summary: Patient screen displaying appointments and test results via a segmented tab (Rendez-vous / Résultats), with navigation to ResultDetailScreen on result tap.

nodes.name: CartScreen.js
nodes.summary: Appointment booking screen with date/slot picker, mode toggle (lab vs home visit), CNAM coverage breakdown, prerequisite questionnaire, GPS capture, and animated confirmation overlay after successful booking.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CommonActions.reset to navigate back to the Bookings tab after booking, avoiding Expo SDK 54 navigation crashes that would occur with a direct navigate call.

nodes.name: HomeScreen.js
nodes.summary: Main patient home screen with unified lab + analysis search (name, city, analysis code), distance/category/CNAM/home-visit filters, a mini Leaflet map (260 px), and a full lab list sorted by relevance.

nodes.name: LabDetailScreen.js
nodes.summary: Lab detail screen showing hero banner, rating, distance, CNAM status, test catalog with category filters, and a sticky footer to navigate to CartScreen with selected tests.

nodes.name: LabMapView.js
nodes.summary: Shared React Native component embedding a Leaflet map in a WebView, supporting lab markers, animated user location, lab popup press callbacks, and both mini-card and fullscreen layout modes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses injectJavaScript to push lab/user updates to the WebView instead of reloading HTML, avoiding Leaflet tile refetch on every re-render. Leaflet tile sizes are also force-invalidated on layout to work around react-native-webview sizing bugs on iOS and Android.

nodes.name: LabMapView
nodes.summary: Default-exported component that manages a WebView with embedded Leaflet map, synchronizing lab markers and user location via injected JS and exposing an onLabPress callback.

nodes.name: buildHtml
nodes.summary: Generates the full Leaflet HTML string embedded in the WebView, including OSM tiles, CSS marker styles, lab and user marker rendering functions, and invalidateSize hacks.

nodes.name: LoginScreen.js
nodes.summary: Unified login screen supporting email/password, OTP phone flow, Google OAuth, and biometric (Face ID / fingerprint) authentication, with last-identifier prefill and biometric opt-in prompt after first OTP login.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a three-step flow (id → pwd or otp → success) driven by a `step` state. Uses expo-auth-session for Google OAuth and bioStore check before triggering OS biometric prompt.

nodes.name: MapScreen.js
nodes.summary: Full-screen map screen embedding LabMapView in absolute layout, with a floating back header and an animated callout panel at the bottom that appears when a lab marker is tapped.

nodes.name: NotificationsBell.js

tour.title: Project Entry Point
tour.description: The Django management script is the command-line entry point for the entire labConnect backend. It defaults to the dev settings module, which means running any management command — migrations, the dev server, or the custom `runlan` command for LAN-accessible mobile development — starts here. Understanding this file tells you how the backend is bootstrapped and which settings environment is active by default.

tour.title: Infrastructure and Deployment
tour.description: Before reading a single line of application code, it helps to understand how the system is packaged and deployed. The Dockerfile builds a single-stage container image that installs Python and system dependencies (including GeoDjango's GDAL/GEOS libraries), copies the project, and starts Gunicorn on port 8000 as a non-root user. The docker-compose.yml runs a companion PostgreSQL 15 database with a named volume and a pg_isready health check — exactly the PostGIS-enabled database the Django ORM requires. The render.yaml blueprint automates production deployment to Render.com using Supabase Postgres, bridging development containers to cloud hosting without changing application code.

tour.title: Django Settings and App Configuration
tour.description: The split settings package (`base.py` → `dev.py` / `prod.py`) is the control plane for the entire platform. Base.py configures the PostGIS database backend, DRF with RS256-signed JWTs, Celery with Redis, Django Channels for WebSocket readiness, MinIO for file storage, CORS origins, and brute-force protection via django-axes. Dev.py overrides JWT to HS256 (no RSA keys needed locally) and opens CORS to all LAN IP ranges so Expo Go on a phone can reach the backend over Wi-Fi. Prod.py locks everything down with HTTPS-only cookies, HSTS, and WhiteNoise static serving. The root URL configuration in `urls.py` is the single file that wires all app routers under `/api/v1/` and also mounts the Swagger UI and ReDoc endpoints.

tour.title: Shared Data Foundation
tour.description: All Django app models in this project inherit from `core/models.py`'s `BaseModel` abstract class, which provides UUIDs for external IDs (safe to expose in URLs and APIs), a BigAutoField integer for internal primary keys (fast for joins), soft-delete via an `is_active` flag, and an `ActiveManager` that filters deleted records out by default. This single class appears as a fan-in dependency of every domain model in the project — accounts, laboratories, analyses, appointments, inventory, and notifications all build on it. Understanding BaseModel means you understand the structural contract every table in the database honors.

tour.title: Identity and Authentication Models
tour.description: The `accounts/models.py` file defines the identity layer that everything else depends on. The custom `User` model uses phone number as the primary identifier (instead of Django's default username), with email as an optional secondary. `PatientProfile` and `StaffProfile` extend it through OneToOne relationships, keeping patient-specific data (CNAM number, blood type) and staff-specific data (laboratory FK, role) separate from the core auth record. `OTPCode` stores hashed, expiring codes for phone verification. `TrustedDevice` persists biometric device tokens so patients and nurses can log in with Face ID or fingerprint after a first successful OTP verification. The `managers.py` file normalizes phone numbers on creation and supports both regular and superuser flows.

tour.title: Role-Based Permission System
tour.description: The platform supports six roles — `lab_chief`, `biologist`, `technician`, `nurse`, `secretary`, and `patient` — implemented as Django Groups rather than a custom permission model. The `core/permissions.py` file is the most-imported file in the entire backend (fan-in of 8), defining the `HasRole` base class, shortcut permission classes (`IsPatient`, `IsNurse`, `IsLabChief`, etc.), a 2FA verification guard for sensitive staff operations, and the `current_lab_id()` request helper that extracts which lab the JWT bearer belongs to. This file is the keystone of the API security model — every ViewSet uses at least one of its classes. The `seed_roles.py` management command bootstraps these Django Groups from scratch on a fresh install.

tour.title: Authentication API and Services
tour.description: The authentication surface is split across three view files to keep concerns clear. `views.py` handles OTP request/verify for patients, email login for staff, Google OAuth for both roles, and Firebase JWT login for mobile. `views_biometric.py` handles device enrollment and biometric login using the hashed device tokens from `TrustedDevice`. `views_totp.py` handles TOTP 2FA setup for staff via pyotp, including QR code generation for authenticator apps. Behind these views, `services/otp.py` abstracts OTP delivery with pluggable providers (Mock for dev, Twilio SMS or WhatsApp for production), and `services/firebase.py` validates Firebase ID tokens by fetching and caching Google's public RSA certificates.

tour.title: Core Domain Models: Labs, Appointments, Analyses
tour.description: Three models form the heart of the clinical workflow. `laboratories/models.py` defines the `Laboratory` entity with a PostGIS `Point` field for geospatial queries, a JSON `opening_hours` field, home-visit fee settings, CNAM support flag, and a slug. `appointments/models.py` builds on `BaseModel` and references both `Laboratory` and `User`, adding `VisitType` (clinic vs. home) and `AppointmentStatus` enumerations, a GIS location field for home visits, an `assigned_nurse` FK, and a fee calculation method. `analyses/models.py` captures the clinical detail: `TestCatalogEntry` defines what tests the lab offers with CNAM coverage and questionnaire support; `Sample` tracks the physical specimen with barcode and lifecycle status; `TestOrder` links a test to an appointment with CNAM cost split; `TestResult` stores the technician-entered value and biologist-validated result with a full audit trail.

tour.title: API Layer: ViewSets and Serializers
tour.description: The API layer exposes the domain models to clients through DRF ViewSets paired with serializers. `analyses/views.py` is the most complex ViewSet (fan-out of 5), implementing catalog management, sample reception, result entry, biologist validation, patient result listing, PDF streaming, walk-in registration, statistics, and invoice generation — all role-gated via `core/permissions.py`. `appointments/views.py` handles status-change transitions that cascade: confirming an appointment creates Sample records; completing a home visit triggers nurse assignment logic. The `notifications/events.py` file (fan-in of 2) is called by both the analyses and appointments ViewSets to emit `Notification` records whenever appointment lifecycle events or result validations occur, ensuring all relevant users receive in-app messages without a WebSocket layer.

tour.title: PDF Generation and Result Reports
tour.description: When a biologist validates a test result, the backend can generate a structured A4 PDF using `analyses/pdf.py`, which is built on ReportLab Platypus. The report includes patient identity, the test result value alongside its reference range, a clinical context section, and a biologist signature block. The `analyses/views.py` PDF endpoint streams this file directly to the caller, which on the web dashboard triggers a browser download and on the mobile app is caught by `frontend-client/src/pdfDownload.js`, written to Expo's file cache as base64, and opened in the native share sheet so patients can save, print, or forward their results.

tour.title: Web Staff Dashboard
tour.description: The React 19 + Vite staff dashboard is structured around three pillars that appear in the highest fan-in rankings. `api.js` (fan-in 16) is imported by every screen and component that touches the backend — it owns JWT storage, automatic token refresh on 401 responses, and all domain-specific fetch functions. `constants.js` (fan-in 10) centralizes role definitions, permission maps, and category lists, ensuring role-gating logic is consistent across all screens. `App.jsx` (fan-out 16) is the routing hub: the `Gate` component checks whether the user has a lab assigned (redirecting to `Onboarding.jsx` if not), and the `Shell` component renders the `Sidebar` and `Topbar` layout before delegating to the active screen based on the user's current role.

tour.title: Key Staff Screens: Dashboard and Analyses
tour.description: The two most visited staff screens encapsulate the day-to-day lab workflow. `Dashboard.jsx` shows today's appointment list, allows walk-in creation via `WalkInModal` (which queries the test catalog and handles CNAM configuration), surfaces the `AppointmentDetailModal` for status progression, and embeds `FinanceTab` for daily revenue and CNAM reimbursement tracking. `Analyses.jsx` is where the clinical work happens: technicians enter results through a `ResultEntryModal`, biologists validate them through a `ValidationModal`, and all users can download the PDF report. These two screens together reflect the full appointment-to-result lifecycle that `appointments/views.py` and `analyses/views.py` back on the server.

tour.title: Mobile App: Patient and Nurse Journeys
tour.description: The React Native (Expo 54) mobile app serves two very different users through role-based navigation. `App.js` switches between a patient tab navigator (Home, Bookings, Profile) and a nurse tab navigator (Route, Profile) based on the authenticated user's role. On the patient side, `HomeScreen.js` lets patients search labs by name, city, or analysis code with map-based geo-filtering; `LabDetailScreen.js` shows the test catalog; and `CartScreen.js` handles booking with a date/slot picker, home-visit mode toggle, CNAM coverage breakdown, and a prerequisite questionnaire. On the nurse side, `NurseRouteScreen.js` shows a vertical timeline of today's home visits; `NurseCollectScreen.js` handles per-tube barcode entry; and `NurseValidateScreen.js` closes the visit with a finger-signature canvas backed by `PanResponder` — no external SVG dependency required.

tour.title: Mobile Auth and Biometric Login
tour.description: The mobile authentication layer mirrors the backend's multi-method support. `auth.js` is the React Context provider that wraps the app — it exposes `loginWithOTP`, `loginWithEmail`, `loginWithGoogle`, `loginWithBiometric`, and `logout`, hydrating user state from the backend on mount. Biometric authentication is handled by `biometric.js`, which bridges three Expo packages: `expo-local-authentication` triggers the OS biometric prompt, `expo-crypto` generates a stable device ID, and `expo-secure-store` persists the device token and phone number between sessions. After a patient's first successful OTP login, the app prompts them to enable Face ID or fingerprint for all future logins, using the `TrustedDevice` model on the backend to store the hashed token.

tour.title: Inventory Management
tour.description: The inventory subsystem tracks the lab's reagents, consumables, and equipment through two tightly related models. `inventory/models.py` defines `InventoryItem` (with category, unit cost, minimum stock threshold, and the computed `is_low_stock` property) and `InventoryMovement`, which records signed-delta stock changes atomically using `SELECT FOR UPDATE` to prevent race conditions under concurrent use. The `views.py` enforces role-based access — lab chiefs, technicians, and biologists can add or edit items, but only the lab chief can delete them. On the web dashboard, `Inventory.jsx` presents this as a table with inline `ItemModal` and `MovementModal` for CRUD and stock recording, completing the operational picture that the API model backs.
